newsitem.title: THAILAND: Banpu says lower revenue share from coal.
newsitem.headline: Banpu says lower revenue share from coal.

text.p: Thai coal miner and importer Banpu Plc said on Friday that the proportion of its revenue from its traditional coal business fell this year, while earnings from the sale of electricity and steam grew.
Banpu's revenue from coal and mining accounted for 48 percent of its total income this year, compared with 54 percent last year, Banpu said in a statement.
The proportion of earnings from the sale of power and steam rose to 28 percent of total revenue from 13 percent last year, the company said.
Banpu on Friday announced its net profit for the year ending on June 30 rose to 807.47 million baht from 714.43 million last year. It said profit this year was in line with its projection.
The company's total sales this year were up to 3.1 billion baht from 2.7 billion baht the previous year, it said.
Banpu said a 2.5 billion baht power plant project it was building at the Mab Ta Phut industrial zone in eastern Rayong province was scheduled to be ready in March next year.
